title: Scanned Proton Beam Performance and Calibration of the Shanghai Advanced Proton Therapy Facility
author: Shu, Yin, et al.

steps.title: Configure beamline geometry
steps.instruction: Set up the scanning irradiation system according to the design specifications: place Scan (U) magnet 2.87 m and Scan (V) magnet 2.42 m upstream of the iso‑center; install the 0.1 mm‑thick titanium vacuum window 0.8 m before the iso‑center; locate the primary and secondary dose monitors and the position monitors immediately after the window; if treating shallow skin tumors, insert the discrete range‑shifter plate into the beam applicator and retract the applicator so that the bottom of the applicator is 400 mm from the iso‑center; verify that the lowest extracted beam energy is 70 MeV.

steps.title: Set primary dose monitor parameters
steps.instruction: Apply a high voltage of –2500 V to the parallel‑plate ionization chamber (PPIC) whose electrode gap is 5 mm; confirm that the ion‑charge collection time is <70 µs and the collection efficiency >99%; note that the electronic output is 0.2 pC per count and that one monitor unit (MU) equals 100 000 counts (2 × 10⁻⁸ C); set the allowed MU per spot between 0.005 MU (minimum) and 0.1 MU (maximum).

steps.title: Measure spot size and shape
steps.instruction: For each of the seven energies (70, 130.1, 161.1, 179.9, 202, 219.2, 235 MeV) place a Lynx 2D scintillator (IBA) and a Gafchromic EBT film at the iso‑center in air; record the full‑width at half‑maximum (FWHM) of the spot in the X and Y directions, which should lie between 6 mm and 13 mm; note that at 70 MeV the spot size at 38 mm water depth is ≈14 mm (FWHM) and at 235 MeV at 340 mm depth is ≈18 mm (FWHM).

steps.title: Check lateral profile homogeneity
steps.instruction: Define a calibration field of 60 mm × 60 mm; set spot spacing to 3 mm × 3 mm; using the Lynx detector deliver the field at each of the seven energies listed above; evaluate dose homogeneity across both X and Y directions, requiring better than 5 % (the measurements achieved <2 %).

steps.title: Acquire depth dose distributions
steps.instruction: Place a PTW MP30PL water phantom and a Bragg‑peak parallel‑plate chamber (Model 34070, sensitive volume 10.5 cm³, front‑window water‑equivalent thickness 0.4 cm, effective radius 4.08 cm, electrode gap 2 mm) at the iso‑center; for each energy (70‑235 MeV) move the chamber to successive depths and record the depth‑dose curve; extract the range (g/cm²), entrance‑to‑peak dose ratio, and distal dose fall‑off (DDF 80 %‑20 %) as listed in Table 3; note that the DDF at 235 MeV is <5 mm due to a spill energy spread of ±0.1 %.

steps.title: Test MU delivery reproducibility
steps.instruction: Connect a Bragg ionization chamber (TW34070, PTW) to a UNIDOS‑E electrometer; vary the monitor dose rate from 10 MU/s (high) to 1 MU/s (low); for the high rate deliver 400 spots each receiving 2500 counts, repeat the sequence 14 times; for the low rate deliver 300 spots each receiving 1000 counts, repeat 14 times; calculate the variation of delivered dose, which must be ≤0.1 % for both rates.

steps.title: Assess MU proportionality
steps.instruction: Insert the Bragg‑peak chamber into a PTW plastic phantom at a depth of 15 mm; set the chamber bias to 400 V; for energies 235, 161.1 and 70 MeV deliver spot MU values from 1 to 10 MU in 1 MU steps at dose‑rate settings of 1, 3, 5, 8 and 10 MU/s; record the chamber output (nC/MU) and compute the maximum deviation; the observed deviation must be within ±1 % (see Table 4).

steps.title: Calibrate primary monitor to dose
steps.instruction: Use a Markus chamber calibrated with a 60Co factor from the National Institute of Metrology (China) as the reference dosimeter; follow IAEA TRS‑398 and AAPM TG‑51 procedures; position the chamber at a reference depth Zref = 1.5 g/cm² in water (plateau region of the mono‑energetic beam); adjust the primary monitor to deliver the charge corresponding to 1 MU; repeat the measurement for each pseudo‑mono‑energetic proton beam; perform ten repetitions per energy to achieve reproducibility better than 1 %.

steps.title: Determine monitor calibration factor
steps.instruction: Deliver the 60 mm × 60 mm uniform field with 3 mm × 3 mm spot spacing at each of the seven energies; record the primary monitor reading and the dose measured by the Markus chamber; compute the monitor calibration factor and normalize it to the value at 161.1 MeV; interpolate the factor for the intermediate energies not directly measured.

steps.title: Perform daily QA measurements
steps.instruction: Each day, twice (morning and evening), repeat the monitor calibration measurement as described in the previous step; log the calibration factor; verify that the day‑to‑day variation (one standard deviation) remains <1 %.
